title: This week in recruiting tools: Juicebox buys Fetcher, LinkedIn Hiring Assistant inside iCIMS, Workday ships Candidate Profile and agents
summary: A consolidation week across the recruiting stack: Juicebox agreed to acquire Fetcher's assets, iCIMS wired in LinkedIn's Hiring Assistant, Metaview went deeper into Workday, Workday launched Candidate Profile plus HR agents, Eightfold appointed a new CEO, and Noon published public docs for driving it from AI assistants.

items.headline: Juicebox announced an agreement to acquire Fetcher's assets
items.detail: Announced 6 Oct 2026 (Business Wire; Axios). Fetcher sold batch sourcing on per-role tiers; Juicebox is a natural-language search tool. Fetcher customers should plan for a migration; see Juicebox and Fetcher in the directory and our sourcing-database switching guide.
items.matters: The independent sourcing category keeps shrinking; AI-search vendors are buying customer bases.

items.headline: iCIMS integrated LinkedIn Hiring Assistant into its ATS
items.detail: Announced 14 Oct 2026 (HRTech Series), two weeks after LinkedIn's 'Hiring Assistant 2' update (TLNT, 2 Oct), which focused on smarter matching.
items.matters: LinkedIn's agent now lives inside a major enterprise ATS, so iCIMS customers get an agent without adding a vendor; the seat and InMail credit model is unchanged. Compare in iCIMS and LinkedIn Recruiter.

items.headline: Metaview expanded its Workday integration for Fortune 500 recruiting teams
items.detail: Announced 14 Oct 2026 (Business Wire). Metaview records and structures interviews and is extending that into agentic workflows on Workday data (Metaview review).
items.matters: The ATS is becoming the control plane for recruiting agents; point tools without native Workday or SAP integrations will feel it in enterprise deals.

items.headline: Workday launched Candidate Profile and a set of HR, finance and IT agents
items.detail: Announced 13 Oct 2026 (Workday blog; Investing.com). Candidate Profile is a reusable applicant profile meant to end repeated form-filling.
items.matters: Portable profiles change the apply experience for the largest employers, and Workday's own agent layer now competes directly for third-party automation budget.

items.headline: Eightfold AI named Joe Korngiebel as CEO
items.detail: Announced 13 Oct 2026 (GlobeNewswire). Eightfold sells talent intelligence, matching and rediscovery to large enterprises.
items.matters: CEO changes at platform vendors usually precede packaging and pricing changes; buyers mid-evaluation should ask about the roadmap and contract flexibility.

items.headline: Noon published public MCP docs, a weekly changelog and switch-from guides
items.detail: Published 14 Oct 2026 (noon.ai/changelog). The docs let Claude and ChatGPT users drive Noon's sourcing and outreach tools from their assistant.
items.matters: First vendor in our directory with public AI-assistant (MCP) documentation; expect 'can my assistant run it?' to become a standard RFP line.

directory: New on BestRecruitmentTools.com this week: vendor-neutral switching guides for teams leaving LinkedIn Recruiter, SeekOut or hireEZ and Gem.

title: This week in recruiting tools: Dayforce goes agentic with Ribbon inside, Gap hires with Paradox, iCIMS tops UX scores again
summary: Six stories from a week when HCM suites pulled AI interviewing into the core product. Dayforce rebuilt its recruiting module around agents and Ribbon's interviewer, Gap put a Paradox assistant on top of Workday Recruiting for seasonal hiring, iCIMS kept its spot in an enterprise usability survey, HireVue made the case for structured voice interviews in retail, Deel aimed a security product at fake remote hires, and staffing analysts saw a slow thaw.

items.headline: Dayforce unveiled an agentic HCM platform with a rebuilt recruiting product
items.detail: Reported 1 Nov 2026 (iTWire). The new Dayforce Recruiting adds a candidate CRM plus high volume and contingent hiring workflows, with Ribbon's AI built in for sourcing, rediscovery of past applicants, and voice and video interviews. Dayforce announced its deal for Ribbon on 23 Oct, and says the rollout runs into 2027. Buyers comparing standalone interviewers should read our AI interview tools ranking before signing anything multi-year.
items.matters: When the HCM suite ships an interviewer, standalone vendors have to win on depth, not convenience.

items.headline: Gap launched Bridgette, an AI career guide for store and warehouse applicants
items.detail: Reported 29 Oct 2026 (Retail Dive). Bridgette is built with Paradox on top of Workday Recruiting. It helps applicants find and apply for roles, answers questions, schedules interviews and sends reminders. Gap said a pilot in more than 100 stores and six distribution centers had about 45,000 users and more than 7,000 scheduled interviews. See our Paradox review for how the product is priced and deployed.
items.matters: The retail playbook for seasonal hiring is now a chat assistant over the ATS, not a bigger recruiting team.

items.headline: iCIMS placed in the top five enterprise recruiting providers for user experience for the third year running
items.detail: Announced 4 Nov 2026 (PR Newswire). The ranking comes from Sapient Insights Group's annual HR Systems Survey, which scores vendors on feedback from HR practitioners at organizations with more than 5,000 employees.
items.matters: Usability scores are a reasonable shortlist filter for large ATS buyers, but they say nothing about AI roadmap or pricing; compare those separately in our enterprise ranking.

items.headline: HireVue made the case for structured voice interviews in holiday hiring
items.detail: Reported 5 Nov 2026 (Retail Insider). HireVue pointed retailers at structured two way voice interviews and short job simulations to screen seasonal applicants at volume, paired with transparency to candidates and human review of decisions.
items.matters: Voice screening is moving from pilot to default in hourly hiring, so candidate disclosure language needs to be ready before peak season, not during it.

items.headline: Deel launched Deel Security, aimed at identity fraud in remote hiring
items.detail: Launched 30 Oct 2026 (Enterprise Times). The product targets workforce identity fraud, including fake remote hires who pass interviews under a borrowed identity. It now sits in Deel's product line next to Payroll, HR and IT.
items.matters: Candidate fraud checks are spreading from interview tools into the employer of record layer, which is where identity documents already live.

items.headline: Analysts described a reluctant improvement in staffing demand
items.detail: Reported 2 Nov 2026 (Staffing Industry Analysts), citing UBS analyst Joshua Chan. The note described demand as improving, but slowly and without conviction from buyers.
items.matters: Agencies buying tools this quarter should favor plans that scale down cleanly; see the staffing agency ranking for which vendors bill per seat versus flat.

directory: Also in the directory: rankings for high volume hiring, AI interview tools and enterprise teams, plus reviews of HireVue and Paradox.

title: This week in recruiting tools: Workday folds HiredScore grades into Recruiting, Eightfold ships an AI teammate, Employment Hero bills per placement
summary: Seven dated stories on pricing and rankings. Workday put AI grading inside its core recruiting screen, Eightfold pitched an agent that owns a hiring goal, Employment Hero charged only on placement, HiringDesk.ai published a $199 monthly plan, Talroo collected two third party badges, ZipRecruiter beat guidance, and Payscale measured how far AI is reshaping headcount plans.

items.headline: Workday moved HiredScore grading inside Workday Recruiting
items.detail: Published 12 Nov 2026 (Workday blog). HiredScore's fit and gap grades now appear on the requisition itself, so recruiters can sort applicants by grade and filter on qualifications without a second login. Workday ties the change to volume: its Global Workforce Report counts 69 applications per offer in July 2026, up from 58 a year earlier. The vendor claims screening time falls by half on average; treat that as a vendor figure until your own pilot confirms it. Teams weighing a suite add on against a standalone product can start with our enterprise ranking.
items.matters: AI grading is now a checkbox inside the biggest enterprise suite, which squeezes the price standalone screeners can charge Workday customers.

items.headline: Eightfold introduced AI Recruiting Teammate, a goal driven agent across requisitions
items.detail: Announced 12 Nov 2026 in a paid GlobeNewswire release (via Yahoo Finance). Eightfold says the agent takes a hiring goal and works it from intake to onboarding, following up with candidates over days or weeks while recruiters can review, redirect, pause or take over, with a reviewable log of what it did. The release also points to an independent Local Law 144 bias audit of its matching model by BABL AI. No pricing was published. See how it compares in our Eightfold review and the AI recruiters ranking.
items.matters: Vendors are starting to sell outcomes per requisition instead of a bundle of separate agents, which changes how buyers should compare quotes.

items.headline: Employment Hero reported 30 percent revenue growth and a recruitment agent billed per placement
items.detail: Reported 11 Nov 2026 (Human Resources Director). The Australian HR platform said revenue rose 30 percent and annual recurring revenue passed $400 million. Its recruitment agent charges customers only when a candidate is placed, and it was reviewing more than 600,000 applications a month by July.
items.matters: Success based pricing for software borrows the agency model; if it spreads, seat licenses for small business recruiting tools will face pressure. Compare current options in our small business ranking.

items.headline: HiringDesk.ai launched Ava for local employers, starting at $199 a month
items.detail: Announced 7 Nov 2026 (MarketersMedia via FinancialContent). The Royal Oak, Michigan company says Ava texts applicants, collects short video introductions, scores candidates from 1 to 10 and books interviews without a separate calendar tool. The starting plan includes unlimited locations, a published price point that is rare in this category.
items.matters: A flat, public monthly price undercuts per location quotes from larger high volume vendors. Our restaurant hiring software list covers the incumbents it targets.

items.headline: Select Software Reviews named Talroo among the best job advertising and job posting platforms of 2026
items.detail: Announced 9 Nov 2026 (Business Wire via Rutland Herald). Talroo appears in two Select Software Reviews lists. The reviewer says its picks weigh practitioner recommendations, product demos, customer retention and transparency.
items.matters: Third party lists are increasingly cited in vendor marketing; check the criteria behind any badge before it influences a shortlist.

items.headline: ZipRecruiter beat its own third quarter guidance and raised its full year outlook
items.detail: Reported 9 Nov 2026 (company release via Yahoo Finance). Revenue was $124.4 million, net income $5.1 million and adjusted EBITDA $20.8 million, a 17 percent margin, all above the range the company had guided. Read our ZipRecruiter review for what the paid plans include.
items.matters: A profitable, growing job board has less reason to discount annual contracts, so expect firmer renewal pricing.

items.headline: Payscale found 74 percent of employers expect AI to change headcount plans
items.detail: Reported 11 Nov 2026 (Staffing Industry Analysts). In Payscale's survey, 74 percent of employers said AI would affect headcount or hiring plans, and 40 percent said they struggle to find staff with AI skills.
items.matters: Budgets are shifting from adding recruiters to buying tools, which is the backdrop for every price change above.
